name: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia

criteria.description: Multiple telangiectasias at characteristic sites including lips, oral cavity, fingers, and nose
Visceral arteriovenous malformations (pulmonary, hepatic, cerebral, spinal)
First-degree relative with HHT according to these criteria

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis is definite if 3 or more criteria are present; possible or suspected if 2 criteria are present; unlikely if fewer than 2 criteria are present
diagnosticCriteria.notes: The Curaçao criteria are widely used for clinical diagnosis of HHT.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically on lips, oral mucosa, fingers, and nose

common.notes: Often presents as chronic iron deficiency anemia

occasional.symptomName: Neurological deficits from cerebral AVMs or paradoxical emboli
High-output cardiac failure due to hepatic AVMs

rare.symptomName: Stroke or brain abscess due to paradoxical embolism
Portal hypertension secondary to hepatic AVMs

laboratory: Iron deficiency anemia with low serum ferritin
imaging: Contrast echocardiography or bubble study showing pulmonary AVMs
CT angiography demonstrating AVMs in lungs, liver, or brain
genetic: Mutations in SMAD4 gene (in combined juvenile polyposis-HHT syndrome)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Skin lesions are rubbery blue nodules

redFlags: Sudden onset neurological symptoms indicating cerebral AVM rupture
Severe hypoxemia or cyanosis from pulmonary AVMs
Massive gastrointestinal bleeding causing hemodynamic instability
references: Shovlin CL. Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia: pathophysiology, diagnosis and treatment. Blood Rev. 2010 Mar;24(6):203-19.
Faughnan ME, Palda VA, Garcia-Tsao G, et al. International guidelines for the diagnosis and management of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. J Med Genet. 2011 Feb;48(2):73-87.
Govani FS, Shovlin CL. Hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia: a clinical and scientific review. Eur J Hum Genet. 2009 Jul;17(7):860-71.
